claims.text: The Z method uses a microcanonical ab initio molecular dynamics simulation initialized in a superheated state.
The Z method is more efficient than full ab initio free-energy thermodynamic integration.
The Z method can determine melting properties of refractory materials.
The proposed calculation uses DFT-based molecular dynamics in the microcanonical NVE ensemble.
Heating the simulated material beyond its equilibrium melting temperature induces a spontaneous crystalline-to-liquid transition under constant-energy conditions.
The transition from an ordered crystal to a disordered liquid mediates changes in thermodynamic properties.
A crystal loses stability when it is superheated beyond the melting point.
The latent heat of fusion can be inferred from an abrupt change in the microcanonical energy-temperature curve.
The entropy change at melting can be inferred from an abrupt change in the microcanonical energy-temperature curve.
The volume change at melting can be inferred from an abrupt change in the microcanonical energy-temperature curve.
The Z method should yield the melting temperature with reasonable accuracy relative to free-energy approaches.
The Z method should yield the entropy and enthalpy of fusion with reasonable accuracy relative to free-energy approaches.
The Z method should yield the volume change at melting with reasonable accuracy relative to free-energy approaches.
Superheating in the Z method causes a systematic overestimate of the melting point.
The method is primarily valid for high-melting refractory materials when DFT is reliable and simulation times are sufficient to sample the transition.
Finite-size effects and inherent superheating can affect quantitative agreement between the Z method and full free-energy calculations.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies an NVE simulation, which fixes volume, while later fields propose inferring or observing a volume change at melting. No multi-volume, equation-of-state, or variable-cell protocol is given to reconcile this.
